reference: Euthymios Zigabenos, Panoplia Dogmatica, Tit. XXVIII, sect. 8 (Lat. 8 / Gr. η'), Migne PG 130, cols. 1339–1340
url: Local copy of the 1864 Opera (Google scan), page 694 of the PDF = Migne cols. 1339–1340
gist_en: Mocks the Muslim veneration of the Black Stone (Brachthan) at the Kaaba as idolatry, calling it a statue of Venus or Baccha, and ridicules the rite of circling it.
why_excluded: Its point is to ridicule a religious practice as idolatrous and bizarre (a description of customs as absurd), not a doctrinal argument about Islam's claims; treated as mockery of people's practice under the exclusion rule.

reference: Euthymios Zigabenos, Panoplia Dogmatica, Tit. XXVIII, sect. 1 (Lat. 1 / Gr. α'), Migne PG 130, cols. 1333–1334 (personal clause)
url: Local copy of the 1864 Opera (Google scan), page 691 of the PDF = Migne cols. 1333–1334
gist_en: Describes Muhammad as an ignorant, rustic man (Lat. 'rudis et agrestis homo'; Gr. 'ἀμαθὴς ... καὶ ἀγροικος') who nevertheless wrote 113 fables.
why_excluded: The clause is a personal insult against Muhammad rather than a doctrinal point; the doctrinal part of the same sentence (the 113 fables) is quoted in passage zig_t28_113_fables instead.
